correctness.rationale: Derived inclusion-exclusion exact coefficient formula from cell containment; exhaustive independent bit-mask parity enumerator agrees on every tested selected coordinate set. Width-ten tests exhaust 4525 characters of weight ≤3 and establish exactly 30 third-order zeros, none lower. Half-turn pairing and elementary parity/central-cell proofs establish first occurrence and re-entrance through width fourteen.

evidence: Two-row Young-diagram theorem and two-row Brownian spectral law were read from published RESULT.md; both explicitly restrict to two rows.
Published 2×3×4 boxed plane partitions report a complete 24-bit spectrum, but use a different order-ideal poset from 3×10 (30 bits).
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a result for 2×n nor a one-box result for 2×3×4 covers the 3×10 cell-coordinate transform. General Fourier inversion alone supplies no signed coefficient census. No dominating all-three-row theorem was recovered.

originality.rationale: Archived plane partition and Young lattice literature gives unsigned enumeration, rank statistics or complements, not the fine 3×10 sparse signed spectrum. Closest published two-row Fourier results and a different finite 3D boxed spectrum do not imply the asserted thirty triples or minimal degree; best-knowledge novelty subject to unindexed-equivalence risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier signed enumerator or unpublished cellwise table may recover these sparse coefficients.
A broader 3-row formula may exist outside accessible published-finding corpus and searched primary sources; no universal novelty proof is claimed.

value.rationale: The first cubic-only low-degree Fourier blind spot for a canonical three-row Young lattice has a natural first-occurrence definition, a complete set of 30 exact witnesses and a return to quadratic cancellation at width fourteen. It marks a nonmonotone sparse-recovery boundary not implied by general unsigned counting and is a motivated finite exact invariant rather than an arbitrary slice.
